findings.title: The design builds on 361 artifacts that are not in the tree
findings.description:
- **Missing skill file:** The design says everything is "edits to the existing `commands/analysis/understand.md`" (lines 22, 42, 119-122). `commands/analysis/` contains only `tech-debt-audit.md`.
- **Missing sample:** The design says "943 exists, so expect 944" (lines 367-369, 466-469). `user/analysis/` contains only 940, 941 and 942.
- **No graph:** No `.understand-anything/` directory exists, so the walkthrough's measurements cannot be re-run here.
- **361 not built:** Slice 361's own design is still `status: not_started` and has no implementation.
- **Corrections have nothing to correct:** The two "corrections" are described as defects in shipped skill text, and the 943 sample is cited as carrying "both wrong counts". Neither can be checked.
- **Cheaper alternative:** 361 is unimplemented, so the corrections could be folded into 361's design before it ships, with no correct-then-recorrect sequence.
- **Fix:** The design should state that it depends on 361 being implemented and merged first. Its walkthrough should not hard-code 943 or 944.

findings.title: The design mischaracterizes what 361 specified and deferred
findings.description:
- **Deferral claim:** The design says 361 "explicitly deferred" `config.json`, `.understandignore` and `analyzedFiles` (lines 54-55, 222, 328). Searching `project-documents/user/slices/` finds none of the three named in 361.
- **Selector claim:** The design says 361's skill text "collapsed" the file-level selector to `select(.type == "file")` and "instructs intersecting with `type == "file"`" (lines 121-123, 146-147). 361 specifies `.nodes[] | select(.type == "file" or ...)` (361:108). It says only "each layer's name, description, and file count" (361:244). The elided selector and the unspecified counting method contradict the quoted skill text.
- **Fix:** Reword these as 362 additions, or cite the actual skill text once it exists.

findings.title: The file-level selector is defined three inconsistent ways and departs from the architecture
findings.description:
- **Allow-list or exclusion:** Line 151 says "the file-level selector becomes an explicit type allow-list". The selector at line 155 and the justification at lines 158-159 are an exclusion (`type != function and type != class`).
- **Definition versus test:** The Correction 2 title says file-level means "carries a `filePath`". The selector tests only type. A separate sentence at line 160 adds a drift report for filter survivors with no `filePath`.
- **Departure from the architecture:** The architecture lists nine file-level types (arch:108-110), and the design cites that set (lines 145-146). The exclusion rule admits any other upstream type. The architecture is not updated.
- **False coverage discrepancy:** The coverage section reconciles the filter count against `analyzedFiles` (lines 163-165, 224-227). A non-file type that upstream emits and does not count in `analyzedFiles` would inflate the count. The section would then report a false "graph is internally inconsistent" discrepancy.
- **Fix:** Pick one definition and make the selector, drift check and criterion 5 agree. Either record the deviation from the architecture or use the nine-type allow-list with an unknown-type report.

findings.title: The layer cross-check cannot do what it claims, and drift handling is unspecified
findings.description:
- **Weak test:** The cross-check is "every `nodeIds` entry resolves to a node carrying `filePath`", and a `function`/`class` result is "drift". The architecture's node shape lists `filePath?` on nodes generally (arch:94). The design never establishes that function and class nodes lack it. Only file, config and pipeline nodes are measured to carry it (line 99). If function nodes also carry `filePath`, a function in `nodeIds` passes the test and silently inflates `nodeIds | length`. The check should test type, not `filePath` presence.
- **Dangling ids:** A `nodeIds` entry resolving to no node is not handled. The walkthrough jq has an `UNRESOLVED` bucket (line 353), but the fix text does not.
- **Reporting and continuation:** "Reported as upstream drift" does not say where. It could be the console, the provenance flagged-gaps line, or a stop like 361's malformed-graph failure. The design also does not say whether the layer counts are still emitted when the cross-check fails. The Risk section (lines 439-445) rests on this check.

findings.title: Dependency observations contradict the read discipline and are under-specified
findings.description:
- **Discipline versus criteria:** Section 6 resolves function and class edge endpoints "to their owning file's layer". Doing so needs either function and class node data or parsing the `function:path:name` id prefixes, and the design names neither mechanism. Criterion 9 and walkthrough step 7 require that "no function- or class-level node is read" (lines 332-333, 422-424). The architecture says the same (arch:107-110). Either the read is allowed for this purpose, or the criterion fails.
- **Edge types:** Line 215 limits inter-layer connections to `imports` and `depends_on`. Lines 219-220 then count a `calls` edge between functions as an inter-layer signal. Which edge types count is unclear.
- **Unused field:** `edges[].direction` is listed as required (line 87) but no section uses it.
- **Undefined ordering:** "ties by `weight`" (line 179) does not say how weight combines across many edges between a layer pair (sum, max or mean). It is also unclear whether the primary sort is a count of connections or a count of edge-type totals.
- **Unmapped endpoints:** An endpoint belonging to no layer is not handled. The design asserts full membership only for this graph.

findings.title: "Closing observation" per section is a loophole against the no-third-option rule
findings.description:
- **Contradiction:** The mapping table says a section emits "that fallback and nothing else", and never prose untraceable to its named fields (lines 169-189). Lines 245-250 introduce a prose sentence at the end of every section. That sentence appears in no table row, section detail or success criterion.
- **Subjective test:** The example, "complexity concentrates in the seams where squadron meets an external SDK", is an interpretation. A table of complexity by layer does not directly yield "SDK seams". The "mechanical" test, derivable from the table above, will not reliably separate summary from inference.
- **Conflict with the architecture:** The no-inference goal and the zero-`[INFERRED]` rule depend on this. The simplest consistent choice is to drop the closing observation. The alternative is to restrict it to restating counts and require it to be absent in gap sections.

findings.title: Ordering and fallback rules leave common states unspecified
findings.description:
- **Top tier:** Section 4 says "top ordinal tier". It does not say what happens when no node is `complex`. The top tier could mean the highest tier present or only `complex`.
- **Layer order:** Sections 3 and 4 sort "then layer" with no layer order. Section 2's order (descending count) should be named.
- **Layer ties:** Section 2's count ordering has no tie-break.
- **Empty is not a gap:** Section 6 relies on "preflight rejects empty `edges`". A non-empty `edges[]` can still yield zero inter-layer `imports` or `depends_on` connections, as in a single-layer project. A one-layer graph likewise makes section 2 trivial. The "every section resolves to sourced content or a gap marker" rule (lines 186-189) has no outcome for a legitimately empty result.
- **Missing field versus missing file:** Row 7's fallback names only an unreadable file. A present `meta.json` lacking `analyzedFiles`, or a non-numeric one, is not covered.

findings.title: The `.understandignore` rule contradicts the repo state it cites
findings.description:
- **Contradiction:** Line 234 says "An all-comments file (this repo's current state has 17 active lines) is reported as 'defaults only'". An all-comments file has zero active lines. The verified facts (line 108) and walkthrough spot-check (line 389) expect 17 active patterns to be listed.
- **Missing-file case:** The design does not say whether an absent `.understandignore` is a gap (row 7 says gap) or "defaults only". The config rule at lines 229-231 treats absent upstream optionals as non-gaps.
- **Unbounded list:** "List them" has no bound, which matters for projects with long ignore files.
- **Fix:** Fix the sentence and specify the zero-active-line and absent-file cases.

findings.title: Tour data and the interface to 363/364 are narrower than the plan and architecture assume
findings.description:
- **Tour node IDs dropped:** Section 5 reads only `tour[]` `order`, `title` and `description`. The slice plan has 362 use "`tour[]` ordering as the signal for which components matter most" (plan:89-90). The architecture's concept mapping consumes "`tour[]` node ordering" for Solution Approach, and calls the tour "structured data with node IDs" (arch:99-105, 219). 361 read `nodeIds` (361:246-249). The design drops them, so the document names steps but not the components in them, and 363 cannot reuse them.
- **Mapping does not match 363's needs:** The design says 363 reuses the mapping "verbatim" (lines 36-38, 299-301). The mapping is keyed by comprehension sections. 363 needs concept-section fields: Initial Technical Direction uses `config` nodes (arch:220), and Development Approach uses test/CI `config` nodes (arch:221). Row 1 reads no `config` nodes, so nothing in this slice supplies the Initial Technical Direction and Development Approach inputs.
- **No node ids for 364:** 364 needs "supporting node IDs" (plan:143-146). The document lists file paths, not node ids.

findings.title: The `analyze-codebase-prompt.md` decision says "unchanged" and then edits it
findings.description:
- **Contradiction:** Line 258 says "retain the document unchanged", and line 277 repeats "unchanged". Lines 278-280 and criterion 7 add a cross-reference line.
- **Wording of criterion 11:** The "only changed non-document files" wording (lines 336-338, 434-435) lists a reference document as a non-document file.
- **Inclusion mechanics:** The target file has a pipeline snippet using `{{include:analyze-codebase-prompt.md#system-prompt}}` (reference:227). The design does not say where the note goes, so it could be injected into the system prompt.
- **Metadata:** The reference file's `dateUpdated` (reference:6) goes stale if the file is edited.

findings.title: Walkthrough steps 5 and 6 cannot be run as written
findings.description:
- **Undefined scratch variable:** `$S` is never defined here, and 361 does not define it either.
- **Tampered files not swapped in:** The jq commands write `kg-empty-tour.json`, `kg-no-entrypoints.json` and `meta-wrong.json`. The skill reads `knowledge-graph.json` and `meta.json`, and no step copies the variants over them.
- **Wrong working directory:** The steps `cd` into `.understand-anything` but the skill must run from the scratch project root.
- **Missing scratch inputs:** The scratch copy omits `config.json` and `.understandignore`. The scratch also has no `project-documents/user/analysis/`, so index selection and the write target are unspecified. The coverage section would carry unrelated gap markers beyond the ones being tested.
- **Fragile index:** Step 2's "expect 944" breaks after any re-run. Implementation step 6 says "fixing as found", so each run in the real repo takes the next index and leaves untracked sample documents. Cleanup is not specified.

findings.title: Design weight: unused fields, measured-but-unused facts and rationale embedded in the skill
findings.description:
Cuttable or deferrable scope:
- **Unused fields:** The Interfaces Required table lists `edges[].direction` (no use), `nodes[].tags` for "section grouping" (only the entry-point tag is used) and `tour[].description`. The facts table measures `tour[].languageLesson` (line 106), which no section reads.
- **Optional hotspot annotation:** The `languageNotes` annotation in section 4 (40% coverage, optional omission rule) is optional polish the plan does not require.
- **Rationale in the shipped skill:** Criteria 7 and 8 require the `[INFERRED]` rationale and the reuse decision to be "reflected in the skill" and for the skill to "state why". The skill is installed and loaded on every run. These belong in this design document. The skill needs only the one-line rule ("never emit `[INFERRED]`; use a gap marker").
- **Restatement:** The corrections section restates measurements already in the facts table.
